title: The Weekly Closeout: Target names a new board member and Centric Brands sells itself to CEO
description: The big-box retailer appointed Sally Grimes as an independent director. Meanwhile, Jason Rabin took ownership of the conglomerate.

title: The in-store shopping experience is broken. Can we fix it?
description: Stores still drive retail sales, but self-checkout, locked items and inventory gaps frustrate shoppers. The Modern Retail Podcast breaks down how retailers are attempting to fix these issues.

title: Sally Beauty to expand refreshed store model in 2027
description: The beauty supply retailer will grow the Sally Ignited store concept and has long-term plans to refresh two-thirds of its overall store fleet.

title: Asics uses AI-powered drones to recover misplaced inventory 60% faster
description:
Asics America Corp. is using autonomous drones to find misplaced merchandise at its primary North American distribution center, a move the company says is helping it curb the risk of unfulfilled orders. The technology, developed by Corvus Robotics, is helping the sportswear brand recover misplaced inventory about 60% faster, according to a Nov. 10 announcement […]

title: GrubMarket launches AI Agent to turn invoices into purchase orders
description:

title: AI influencers: What consumer sentiment data tells brands
description: As you scroll through your TikTok or Instagram feed, you’ll no doubt come across at least a handful of influencers trying to sell you something by wearing the latest viral lip gloss, hopping into luxury cars, and taste-testing popular treats. But what if I told you that while these content creators may look like real people, they’re actually AI influencers?

title: The future of CTV lies in standardization
description: Jessica Cobbe, svp, product – supply platform, Nexxen For years, advertisers have focused primarily on in-stream video in CTV, treating the smart TV home screen as secondary real estate. title: Big Box Briefing: How Target’s and Walmart’s beauty department makeovers are reshaping brand strategies
description: As mass-market heavyweights Target and Walmart overhaul their beauty and wellness aisles to rival specialty powerhouses — and each other — large consumer packaged goods companies and independent labels are updating their retail playbooks. Specifically, they’re elevating their look and feel, reallocating their media spending, and rethinking their distribution strategies to best align with retail partners’ directions.
